title: Your Billing Rights — Disputing a Transaction on a Northgate Card Account
content:
**What may be disputed.** A cardholder of a **Northgate Card Credit Accounts (issued by Harbor Point Bank, N.A.)** account may dispute one posted transaction as a billing error: an unauthorized charge, goods or services not received, goods not as described, a return that was not credited, a duplicate charge or an incorrect amount.

**Notice deadline.** Billing-error protections apply only when the dispute notice is received no later than the statement date of the first statement showing the transaction plus the tier's dispute notice days. Calendar days are added to that statement date, the day after it being day 1, and a notice received on the last day still qualifies. The statement date is read from the account record of the first statement on which the disputed transaction appeared.

| Notice received (60-day notice period) | Billing-error protections |
|---|---|
| day 59 after the statement date | apply |
| day 60 after the statement date (the last day) | apply |
| day 61 after the statement date | do not apply |

**The billing-error track.** Such a dispute is opened on the billing-error track: the issuer acknowledges it within the card's acknowledgment days and resolves it within the card's maximum resolution cycles of complete billing cycles and never more than the card's maximum resolution days; while it is open the disputed amount is excluded from the minimum payment and from interest, no late fee arises from leaving it unpaid, and it is not reported as delinquent.

**Late notices.** On Mastercard tiers a dispute about a purchase from a merchant other than Northgate received after that deadline but no later than the transaction date plus the card's network dispute window days is opened on the network-only track, without those protections; on closed-loop tiers and for Northgate purchases a late notice is not accepted.

**One dispute per transaction.** A transaction can be disputed only once; a resolved dispute is not reopened by a new dispute. The account history shows whether a dispute already refers to the transaction.

**Merchant-resolution evidence.** The merchant-attempt requirement applies where the card requires a prior good-faith attempt with the merchant.

- For a Northgate purchase, a not-as-described or returned-not-credited dispute is accepted only when a return of the disputed item is on record with Northgate (the Northgate order the disputed charge paid for shows the return).
- For a Northgate Marketplace purchase, such a dispute is accepted only when a return request to the seller or a Northgate Marketplace Guarantee claim for the order is on record, and opening the dispute closes any guarantee claim on that order under the Northgate Marketplace Guarantee eligibility rules.
- For other merchants the cardholder's account of a good-faith attempt to resolve it with the merchant is accepted.

**Outcomes.** A dispute is resolved for the cardholder when the investigation confirms the error, for the merchant when it does not, and withdrawn when the cardholder withdraws it or the merchant credits the transaction in full first.

**Resolution limits.** If a billing-error dispute is not resolved within the limits, the cardholder keeps up to 50.00 USD of the disputed amount even if the charge proves correct.
